- When sentiment is consistently negative or neutral over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast bias by 5–10% below historical mean.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75.00), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply dampening factor of 0.85 to forecasted peaks.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., >0.67 for 3+ days), model frequently overestimates near-term upside; cap forecast at +10% above recent 7-day average.
- When sentiment turns negative after a peak, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 14-day moving average if sentiment drops below 0.33.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price if sentiment is weak or flat; add 3–5% upward bias if sentiment < 0.33 for 5+ days.
- If sentiment is mixed or volatile (alternating +/–), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast using 5-day weighted average to reduce erratic swings.
